name: Ferguson Middle School
notes: Continuous secondary-school lineage at 701 January Ave: built with WPA assistance and opened 1939 as Ferguson High School (400 students transferred from John M. Vogt High School, per Living New Deal and Wikipedia's McCluer HS history); after Ferguson High's last graduating class in 1962 the building became Ferguson Junior High, later renamed Ferguson Middle School. The rename year is not documented online, but the 'Ferguson Middle School' name is attested by 1989 (a 1989 yearbook 'documenting the school's rebuilding following a fire that swept through the west wing in 1988,' per flovalleynews.com). opened_year therefore records the 1962 conversion of the building to a junior-high/middle entity; the 1939 building opening and the 1962 high-school closure belong to the predecessor rows (Ferguson High School = ALL-416, Ferguson Junior High = ALL-418, both in batch 14). Still operating today (NCES 291201000462; fms.fergflor.org). A 1952 cornerstone/time capsule placed by the 8th-grade class of 1953 was rediscovered after the 1988 fire.

name: Vogt High School
notes: The 1948 Ferguson High 'Crest' yearbook (e-yearbook.com scan) is the primary source: the Community Hall Association donated the site in 1930 and the John M. Vogt High School — the district's first building used strictly for high school students — was erected and named for board member/treasurer John M. Vogt; high school students transferred from Central School. AS&U and STLPR corroborate 'opened in 1930 as a high school with 220 students.' Seed's 'Opened Sept. 9, 1931' likely reflects a dedication date or the Ittner building's 1931 completion date (Wikipedia's W. B. Ittner works list); the first 'Crest' yearbook appeared in 1931. Closed as a high school in 1939 when students moved to the new Ferguson High School at 701 January Ave (ALL-416, batch 14). The Vogt building itself continued as Vogt Junior High (ALL-421) and later Vogt Elementary until 2019, so the *entity* had no closure — only the high-school function ended.

name: Vogt Junior High School
historical_names: John M. Vogt High School (same building, 1930-1939)
Vogt Elementary School (same building, later years)
notes: Vogt became the junior high when the new Ferguson High School opened in 1939 (confirmed). Seed asserts the junior high closed in 1981 — i.e., conversion to Vogt Elementary — but no online source pins that year; left unknown rather than fabricate. What is confirmed: the school operated as Vogt Elementary at 200 Church St until the FFSD board's Oct 10, 2018 redistricting vote closed it at the end of the 2018-19 school year (STLPR, AS&U, St. Louis American); students were absorbed into restructured preK-2/3-5 primaries and sixth-grade centers — no single successor school. publicschoolreview.com lists 'Closed 2020,' which is the NCES record-year for the 2019 closure. Recommended human follow-up: FFSD 'History of Ferguson' (1975) or board minutes to pin the JH-to-elementary conversion year.

name: Central School - Early Ferguson School
district_operator: Ferguson Public School District (District #3) / Ferguson-Florissant R-II
notes: ROW CONFLATES TWO THINGS (flagged, not merged): the Ferguson's first one-room school (opened 1867 at SW corner of Wesley Ave & N. Florissant Rd — the seed's 1867 open / 1880 close refers to this building being replaced) AND the brick 'Ferguson School' at 201 Wesley Ave. Per the 1984 NRHP nomination (NPS 84002706): trustees bought 2.5 acres May 25, 1877; the brick schoolhouse was built 1877-80 (Scharf's 1883 history says erected 1877-78; completion possibly 1880). STLPR and the St. Louis Post-Dispatch Suburban Journal both state the school 'opened in 1880.' It hosted a two-year high school course from ~1894-96 and became one of the county's first accredited four-year public high schools in 1903 (NRHP + 1948 Crest yearbook). It was renamed 'Central School' when Vogt High opened — the NRHP gives ~1931-32 via county directories; Wikipedia says 1903; NRHP is the stronger source. Additions 1895, 1904, 1908 (Wilbur T. Trueblood), 1925-27. NRHP-listed 1984. STLPR calls it 'the oldest school in north St. Louis County.' Still operating as Central Primary (K-2) at 201 Wesley Ave. The 1867 building was expanded and moved to 110 S. Clark, where it survives as a residence (NRHP).

name: Griffith School
opened_citation: Seed attributes 1927 to the FFSD-compiled 'History of Ferguson' (1975); school confirmed operating by Jan. 24, 1967 via St. Louis Post-Dispatch tornado photo cited in https://www.stlpr.org/health-science-environment/2011-04-25/twister-damages-elementary-school-in-ferguson
notes: Still operating as Griffith Elementary (grades 3-5), 200 Day Drive, Ferguson (NCES lists 292 students). Seed's 'Chambers Road' is consistent — Day Drive fronts the school property off Chambers near the city core. The 1927 founding date itself has no direct online citation; it comes from the district-compiled history (not online) and is plausible: the school stood by Jan 1967 when an F4 tornado tore the roof off its gym/cafeteria (Post-Dispatch photo), and the Apr 22, 2011 Good Friday tornado damaged the same roof, closing it for the remainder of that school year (reopened Aug 2011 per Patch). Likely named for W. W. Griffith, Ferguson superintendent 1902-1930 (1948 Crest yearbook) — inference, not verified. Per FFSD's April 2025 board plan, Griffith will 'transition to the Restoration & Wellness location' in the 2027-28 restructuring — watch for a status change.

name: Vernon School - Ferguson Campus
district_operator: Ferguson Public School District / Ferguson-Florissant R-II
notes: STLPR (drawing on the Ferguson Historical Society's 'Ferguson: A City and Its People,' 1976, and district historian interviews): the Ferguson school board built Vernon in 1885 for African-American children — a small frame building on a one-acre lot south of the train station (the seed's 'Florissant Road/Farachi Pizza site' area). Grades 1-8; Black high-school students were sent to Douglass High School in Webster Groves. It closed frequently in early years when enrollment fell below the state minimum of 10. In 1927 the district built a NEW brick Vernon School at the western edge of the district for Black students from Ferguson and Kinloch Park. Vernon remained all-Black until it closed in 1967 — 13 years after Brown v. Board — at which point students were absorbed into desegregated Ferguson-Florissant schools; no single successor. IMPORTANT DEDUP FLAG: this is a different school from Kinloch's Vernon School (ALL-396 / ALL-397, batch 13) — the deduped_review_needed file already pairs them; keep separate.

name: Lee-Hamilton Intermediate School
notes: Resolved seed's Unknown: the official FFSD Lee-Hamilton Family Handbook (2025) states 'Lee-Hamilton Intermediate, established in 1950, is named after Arthur Lee and Sarah Hamilton, two prominent figures in education in North County.' Currently serves grades 3-5 at 401 Powell Ave, Ferguson (FFSD 2023-24 directory; NCES). Slated to become a K-5 elementary in the district's 2027-28 restructuring.

name: Johnson-Wabash 6th Grade Center
notes: Current sixth-grade center at 685 January Ave (adjoining the Ferguson Middle campus), created in the Oct 2018 board restructuring that took effect for the 2019-20 school year — AS&U: 'Sixth grade centers will open on adjoining middle school campuses.' Wikipedia/FFSD list it as 'formerly Johnson-Wabash Elementary School.' The predecessor elementary's own lineage (Johnson School / Wabash School merger) is covered by seed row ALL-406 (batch 14) — this row covers the 6th-grade-center entity. Per the April 2025 board plan, Johnson-Wabash reverts to a K-5 elementary in 2027-28.

name: McCluer Junior High School
notes: Seed confirmed: opened as a junior high in 1957 and became McCluer (Senior) High School in 1962 when Ferguson High School closed and its students moved to McCluer — same building at 1896 S. New Florissant Rd, still operating today as McCluer High School (seed row ALL-111, batch 5). Confidence on opened_year is 'probable' rather than 'confirmed' because Wikipedia's article is internally inconsistent (infobox 'Established 1957' + history text 'opened in 1957 as a junior high school' vs. pre-history line 'When McCluer opened in 1958'). Named for Virgil C. McCluer, Ferguson superintendent 1930-c.1948 (1948 Crest yearbook). Note: seed's ZIP-63135 inclusion is community-served only — actual address ZIP is 63031 (Florissant).

name: STEAM Academy at McCluer South-Berkeley High
historical_names: STEAM Academy at McCluer South-Berkeley High School
McCluer South-Berkeley High School (predecessor program in same building)
notes: Resolved seed's Unknown: the FFSD board voted 4-2 on Oct 10, 2018 to convert McCluer South-Berkeley High into a selective STEAM magnet (STLPR/Wikipedia); the Flo Valley News reported STEAM Academy opened to students Thursday, Aug 15, 2019. Same building at 201 Brotherton Ln — opened January 2004 as McCluer South-Berkeley HS on the former Berkeley High School site (Berkeley HS closed 2004; the MSB entity is seed row ALL-113, batch 5). This is a conversion/rebranding, not a closure: district-wide selective enrollment, grades 9-12, 'Bulldogs' athletics retained (football dropped). Still operating.

name: North County Technical High School
district_operator: Special School District of St. Louis County
notes: SEED OPERATOR CORRECTION: this is not a Ferguson-Florissant R-II school — 'North County Technical' was the early name of North Technical High School (North Tech), the county-wide vocational high school operated by the Special School District of St. Louis County at 1700 Derhake Rd, Florissant (ZIP 63033). SSD's official history (appliedtech.edu): SSD moved into technical education in 1966, opened South Tech in 1967 and North Tech the following year — i.e., 1968; MapQuest profile also gives 'Founded in 1968.' The school appears as 'North County Technical High School (North Tech)' in the 1980-87 Liddell desegregation litigation (8th Cir. opinions). Still open serving grades 10-12. Included in the batch because Ferguson-area students attended — correct per seed's intent, but ZIP attribution is community-served only.

name: St. Louis Community College - Florissant Valley Student Publications
historical_names: St. Louis Community College - Florissant Valley
district_operator: St. Louis Community College (Junior College District of St. Louis-St. Louis County)
notes: ROW-TYPE FLAG: this is a publications-search row for the Florissant Valley campus entity, not a distinct school — it refers to the same institution already researched as pilot row 63147-11 (and duplicated by ALL-444/ALL-445 in this batch). Retained per the no-silent-merge rule. Timeline: Junior College District approved by voters April 1962; classes began January 1963 in temporary quarters (including McCluer HS); permanent 3400 Pershall Rd campus built 1966 (Wikipedia) and opened for the 1967-68 year (earliest FV yearbook is 1967-68; May 1967 cornerstone documented, per pilot research). Campus renamed from 'Florissant Valley Community College' to 'STLCC-Florissant Valley' format in 1976. Campus remains open.

name: St. Louis Community College - Florissant Valley - Former St. Louis County Junior College
historical_names: St. Louis County Junior College District
Junior College District of St. Louis-St. Louis County
district_operator: St. Louis County Junior College District (officially: Junior College District of St. Louis-St. Louis County)
notes: ENTITY RESOLUTION (administrative-sounding name): 'St. Louis County Junior College (District)' is the informal name for the Junior College District of St. Louis-St. Louis County — the district IS the college, not a layer above separate yearbook-producing schools, so treated as the institutional predecessor of STLCC (entity_type individual_school). District established by voter referendum in April 1962 (the ERIC case study documents its formation); classes began January 1963 in temporary quarters. SEED ERROR: 'Closed 1965' is wrong — the district never closed; it continues today as St. Louis Community College (established 1962 per Wikipedia/STLCC). The 1965 date likely reflects the $47.2M bond issue that funded the permanent campuses (per pilot research). The FV campus opened 1966-67 at 3400 Pershall Rd.

Junior College District of St. Louis-St. Louis County

name: St. Peter School
district_operator: Archdiocese of St. Louis (per seed; unverified)
notes: UNRESOLVED / LIKELY MISATTRIBUTED ROW: found no evidence of a Catholic 'St. Peter School' located in Ferguson (63135). NCES Private School Universe Survey and St. Louis Catholic school directories list no such Ferguson school. What does exist: (a) Ferguson's Catholic parish schools were Our Lady of Guadalupe (operated ~70 years; closed end of 2024-25 per Dec 2024 archdiocesan announcement) and Blessed Teresa of Calcutta (parish formed 2005 by merging Good Shepherd, Sts. John & James, St. Bartholomew, St. Sebastian, Our Lady of Fatima and North American Martyrs; its school closed ~2010 per stltoday); (b) St. Peter's United Church of Christ at 1425 Stein Rd, Ferguson — a Protestant (German Evangelical) congregation that relocated to Ferguson via a 1957 mission chapel and consolidated there in 1973; it DID erect 'a school and chapel' at its earlier St. Louis Ave & Warne site in the City of St. Louis in 1906 (StLGS congregation history), but that was not in 63135 and no Ferguson day school is documented; (c) St. Peter's Catholic School in Kirkwood (215 N Clay Ave, ZIP 63122) and St. Peter Catholic School, Jefferson City — plausible seed referents but outside this ZIP. Recommended human follow-up: check the source spreadsheet's intent and Archdiocese of St. Louis parish-history records before spending Track B effort.
